$comment: Ship part catalogue. Masses in kg, thrust in N, Isp in s, torque in N*m. Sizes are in grid cells; one cell is 1 metre. Drag is derived from the ship's frontal width, so only parts that deliberately add drag carry extra_drag_area. Balanced against tools/refsim - see docs/BALANCE.md.

parts.name: Corvid Mk1 Capsule
parts.description: Houses the flight computer. Every ship needs exactly one.

parts.name: Wren Probe Core
parts.description: A capsule with the crew, windows and most of the mass removed. Lighter, and no less clever.

parts.name: FT-05 Tank
parts.description: Propellant, in the smallest useful quantity.

parts.name: FT-11 Tank
parts.description: The workhorse. Better dry-to-wet ratio than two smalls.

parts.name: FT-32 Tank
parts.description: 4 tonnes of propellant, and the best dry-to-wet ratio in the bay. Enough to reach orbit and argue about it afterwards.

parts.name: Kestrel Booster
parts.description: Heavy, thirsty, and the only thing here that will lift you off Halcyon. 120 kN at 300 s.

parts.name: Halo Vacuum Engine
parts.description: Efficient but weak: 40 kN at 345 s. Wonderful in orbit, useless on the pad.

parts.name: Pip Vernier
parts.description: For the small, precise corrections that decide a rendezvous.

parts.name: RW-4 Reaction Wheel
parts.description: Turns the ship without spending propellant.

parts.name: RW-12 Reaction Wheel
parts.description: Three times the authority. Worth it on anything long and heavy.

parts.name: Strut Section
parts.description: Connects things. Adds mass and inertia, which is sometimes the point.

parts.name: Ablative Shield
parts.description: Quadruples the ship's drag area. Pointed the right way it turns an atmosphere into a brake; pointed the wrong way it is ballast.

parts.name: Landing Legs
parts.description: Survives touchdown up to 12 m/s. Without them, any contact is a crash.
